Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
Sure, it's unscientific, but it makes me feel better!

------------------------------------------------------
So far, we have:

Pro-Ban. Taking this position means that you generally feel that
banning cards is favorable to drastically changing the card's text.

Anti-Ban. Taking this position means that you feel that changes to card
text are preferred to banning.

Undecided. Taking this position means that you are, well, undecided.
If you see your name here, but you really _are_ decided, let me know.
In fact, if I have incorrectly interpreted your position and put you on
the wrong list, let me know.

poster does not use their real name, to aid in identification. If
anyone objects to this, let me know.

Messages.Author: LSJ

> Right now the count is 16-5-3. Looks like a LOT of people are in favor
> of just banning cards instead of making such complex changes. LSJ, your
> thoughts?

Nice little survey.

As more information continues to come in, I will be able
to evaluate the situation more fully.

If problems with the errata persist, then changes will
have to be made, naturally.

But still, tournament-level banning is in the domain of
the VEKN and the DCI, not the RT. I wouldn't recommend
that they impose a ban at this point, obviously.

Thanks for handling this in a level-headed way.

--

So why not let people make up their own house rules to fixing

Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
ernie&jeanine wilson wrote:
>
> O.K. , There is your list. Here are my counters. (See below)

In a game where "counterspell" (or whatever you want to call it) exists,
of course this can be used to thwart any broken card. But the existence
of a counterspell does not justify the existence of the broken card, or
make that card any less broken. Before the release of Sabbat, this game
did not have a counterspell. Nor did it need such a card. It seems to
me that some people on the design team felt as you do; that the
existence of such a card would allow them to design other overpowered
cards. But this is not in the spirit of this game. Direct Intervention
hurts the game, and hence should be banned.

> > I believe that the cards most people would want to see discussed for
> > banning include:
> >
> > Tomb of Ramses III
> SUDDEN REVERSAL, ARSON

Please no need to shout. Sudden Reversal is always a factor with Master
cards, and again does not justify making them overpowered. Even if you
Arson the Tomb on your turn, the Tomb user has already gained 1 pool and
four free transfers.

> > Return to Innocence
> DIRECT INTERVENTION, ARCHON INVESTIGATION, AND INTERCEPT

See my above comments on DI. Archon Investigation is another card which
most likely should not have been printed and/or needs to be banned; I
forgot to put it on my list. Intercept will not help if the action is
made to be unblockable. And before you mention it, not everyone can
play with bleed bounce.

> > Direct Intervention
> WHY WOULD YOU BAN THIS ? , ...... SUDDEN REVERSAL

See my above comments on DI.

> > Mind Rape DIRECT INTERVENTION, AND INTERCEPT

See my above comments on DI. The fact that an action can be blocked is
not an excuse for it to be unbalancingly powerful.

> > Thoughts betrayed
> For me the varried nature of V:tes decks is the thing that keeps it
> interesting. By banning cards you will dillute the flavor of the game.

Varied is good. Overpowerful is bad.

Messages.Author: CPilh...@bhak12.ac.at
Messages.Body:
> just...@my-dejanews.com wrote in article
> <6o4cd9$3n$1...@nnrp1.dejanews.com>...

> > > Right now the count is 16-5-3. Looks like a LOT of people are in favor

Well, I'm indecisive, but I rather tend to not ban cards.

But I don't like that new cards are "created" out of existing ones.

Leave the cards the way they are, or at least modify them only
slightly.

What I like:
- aggro rule
- D-bleed only your prey (with exceptions)
- golden rule of card-ownership

What I don't like:
- D-actions allowed against oneself
- Wake-ruling
- Pulled Fang-ruling (7/7)
- Rewriting ToR, RtI, MR (though I wouldn't mind *minor* adjustments)
- Fame ruling
- Zip gun ruling

What I'm not sure about:
- vote pushing rule
- TB ruling (that's not so hard)
- DI discussion

Okay, I think these are the major points.

Let me state this: in general, I think LSJ does a good job. But
the (7/7)-rulings were a bit rash. Some of them are a bit weird
(esp. WwEF!!) for seasoned players. I have the *impression* these
are houserules of LSJ. While some of the new rulings are debatable,
some are definitly wrong for V:TES (like WweF or PF).

I could live with most of the new rules. The point is: too much rulings
in too few time! This is a very sensitive area, quick fixes and changes
do the game great harm!

-Carl



> Well, I'm indecisive, but I rather tend to not ban cards.

Do you guys still use 4CL and a 2CL on certain cards?

Me, either. My only real complaint with the new rulings. Minor
wording changes are a lot easier to remember and can be explained
as typos to newbies.

> What I like:
> - aggro rule

I like it, too, but could be hard to teach. Minor problem, really.

> - D-bleed only your prey (with exceptions)

What this really does is force a little variety in a bleed deck.

> - golden rule of card-ownership

Yeah, I always liked in Vienna how cards stayed around after someone
was ousted. The big problem, IMHO, is that a lot of American players
have bad attitudes and "want to take the ball and go home" when they
lose.

> What I don't like:
> - D-actions allowed against oneself

There really are only a few to worry about. Plus it elliminates a lot
of errata.

> - Wake-ruling

It will now be used primarily in Deflection decks. Forced Awakening
will be used by decks that actually want to get into combat.

> - Pulled Fang-ruling (7/7)

It really is hard enough to do more damage than the other vampire.
At least in the groups I've played in. That's why I like my Assamite
deck the most: Blood Sweat baby. :)

> the (7/7)-rulings were a bit rash. Some of them are a bit weird
> (esp. WwEF!!) for seasoned players. I have the *impression* these
> are houserules of LSJ.

I think the problem here is the interaction between the RT and the
DCI/V:EKN tournament stuff. The DCI/V:EKN should ban cards that are
overpowered in tournaments. The RT should be focused on eliminating
ambiguity and determining what happens in weird situations. Anything
else should be up to individual groups.

Mike

Messages.Author: Alan Flesch
Messages.Body:
<Snip>

First, a small treatise on 'Trump Cards'.

I object to the presence of cards which counter opponants'
plays without game interactions. The simulation presented
in Jyhad was the interaction of Methuselahs (behind-the-
scenes manipulators) via minions (front-line warriors and
schemers).

Master Cards were represented as the 'boons' of the Methuselahs
to their minions. These could represent resources of the
cities, special benefits, or other power-structure forming.
Sudden Reversal was created to counter these Methuselah
Boons on the same level on which they are granted. In most
cases, the Master Cards are strategic cards which represent
the establishment of a battlefield, rather than being actual
tactical advantages (though these strategic resources may
have tactical advantages eg. Elysium). However, the
interaction of Methuselah-to-methuselah was limited
to this level alone.

The majority of the game is played on the minion-to-minion
level. That is, there should be no possible way for a player
with no minions to achieve victory. It is necessary for these
minions to interact in some fashion -- this is the level on
which the Game-qua-game is played. The Master Phase
establishes the battlefield, but the Minion Phase enacts
the battles.

Direct Intervention violates this minion-to-minion interaction by
countering minion activities without interaction. The game
is 'bypassed' for advantage rather than playability. Since the
majority of the game takes place during the minion phase, cards
which prevent/counter minion interaction destroy the fabric
of playability. Yes, it's advantageous to nullify your opponants'
strategies by Direct Intervention, but this violates the fundamental
principles upon which the game was created.

Even from a 'storyline' perspective (I am also an L5R player) the
multiplicity of Direct Intervention violates the premisse. A
methuselah shouldn't dirty its hands directly in the activities
of its minions, except in grave circumstances. The repeatablity of
Direct Intervention lessens the 'omnipresence' mystique of the
Methuselah until they become somewhat similar to Bond Villains
rather than Illuminati.

I could permit Direct intevention if it received the same kind of text
as Giants' Blood (may only be played once per game; if nullified,
it still counts as having been played) to simulate the gravity of a
Methuselah who comes forth from the shadows to protect a valued
minion. It would move the card from the realm of humdrum
everyday-ness to a real Event.

The presence of a powerful trump card also has an effect on how
other cards are viewed. No card can be considered abusive, because
a trump card exists. It's a vicious cycle. Direct Intervention was
created to counter terribly constructed cards such as Return to
Innocence or Thoughts Betrayed. It becomes necessary to counter
these overpowered cards; however, the presence of a countermeasure
card now 'justifies' having such overpowered cards! "It's not that
powerful -- it can be countered with Direct Intervention!"

Sudden reversal doesn't bother me as much, simply because Master
Cards do represent behind-the-scenes operations; there is already
very little interaction between Methuselahs themselves; countering
the activities of a Methuselah off-screen doesn't violate the
premisse of the game. The problem with the card arises with the
'countermeasure justifies powerful Master Cards' problem described
above.

> > Tomb of Ramses III SUDDEN REVERSAL, ARSON

To counter the Tomb, one has to rely on a trump card. I don't like
that premisse in gameplay, so I'll set it aside for the moment.

By the time Arson can be played, the Meth has already recouped
his loss and even gained some effective pool (since he didn't have
to pay the extra pool, but ends up with a larger vamp, he
has gained 'effective' pool).

> > Return to Innocence DIRECT INTERVENTION, ARCHON
> > INVESTIGATION, AND INTERCEPT

DI : Trump Card. 'nuff said.

Archon Investigation : An overpowered countermeasure to an
Overpowered problem. The Card was necessary to counter
unblockable ultrableeds. When RtI was released, this card
became a had-to-have card (it took me months to get mine).
Now, any deck that doesn't play with it is hosed. I don't like
being forced to construct 1/4 of my deck before I even have a
concept. (Direct Interventions/Sudden Reversals/Archon Investigations).

Intercept : Most of the problem with RtI is that it can be made
unblockable : Day Operation (the most common route), Misdirection/
The Sleeping Mind (A popular Dominate combo since RtI can
then be boosted with bleed modifiers) If RtI could be used not
permitting modifiers, it _might_ be playable...

Bleed-bounce : (not mentioned) - This necessitates every player
playing with Dominate (since most of the Bleed-bounce exists
here). I like versatility and flexibility in games, not ones that
demand particular playing styles.

> Direct Intervention WHY WOULD YOU BAN THIS ? , ...... SUDDEN REVERSAL

See my diatribe above on why I dislike Countermeasure cards.

> > Mind Rape DIRECT INTERVENTION, AND INTERCEPT

Again, intercept has taken some big hits against unblockability.

> If you have all of the skills you should be able to deal with those
> cards, they're easy.

Skill is set aside with such cards as Direct Intervention, Sudden
Reversal, or unblockable actions. What skill is present in relying
on directly countermeasuring your opponants' tactics?

What you should say is "If you have all the cards you should be
able to deal with those cards, they're easy." Reliance on two
all-purpose no-drawback counter-measures for all your deck's
defense is just bad game design.

>This next one is a bit tougher, but again I say
> DIRECT INTERVENTION. I can not understand why you
> would want to ban such a versitle card as DI.

Because it justifies a power-escalation which crept into the game
over time. The presence of the two counter-cards which were
created to re-balance the game have thrown the power-curve
way up, since now there is no card which cannot be justified as
being "easy to counter". Because Direct Intervention betrays the
whole premisse of the game (no, I can't spell Premisse. I could
look it up, but then I'd lose my train of thought) that interaction
between minions is a good thing. Because it is a substitute for
strategy and rather relies on brute-force denial in an elegant game
of action/reaction. Because it smacks of 'there is no problem,
look at this card!' solutions to real problems which were added
to a very simple design.

> Thoughts betrayed
> For me the varried nature of V:tes decks is the thing that keeps it
> interesting. By banning cards you will dillute the flavor of the game.

I would love to dilute the game by banning Direct Intervention.

Alan (aj)

Messages.Author: Alan Flesch
Messages.Body:
gen...@iname.com wrote:
>
> > Direct Intervention
>
> Pardon my ignorance, but why is it one a problem?
>

> It does something similar to Sudden Reversal,
> except that it targets a minion card and cost 1 pool.

I just wrote a diatribe against the card. Here are the
highlights...

I : Storyline/Game Design Argument

Jyhad is a game where Methuselahs use minions
to try to destroy their rivals.

Master Cards represent the actions of the Methuselahs
to give their minions advantages. These are largely
strategic items rather than tactical. There is little
interaction between Meths; Sudden Reversal is
one of the few Meth/Meth interactions in the game.
Very little a Master Card can do will affect another
Meth (it is the violation of this principle which makes
Fame such a lethal card).

Minion Cards represent actions between minions.
The game is largely played on this level, with
minions acting to carry out the whims of their masters.
The game consists of the acting player trying to act,
and the minions trying to counter those actions with
reactions of their own (stealth/intercept, political
actions/voting blocs, etc).

Direct Intevention has the Meth interacting in the
Minion level. There is no interaction between minions.
There is no gameplay. There is only the great
NO.

It violates the division between minion/Meth. It
violates the gameplay scenario. It violates the
inscrutability of the Meths (especially since multiple
DI's can be played serially). It violates the
idea of the game.

II. The Justifiability of Power

The presence of DI is seen as the ultimate justification
of Overpowered cards. Remove the 'Just use Direct
Intervention' argument, and suddenly the discussions
on countermeasures become increasingly convoluted and
of questionable use. There is no card which cannot
be justified by the existence of DI ( a card which was
_created to counter_ overpowered cards in the first place).

Alan (aj)

Messages.Author: Alan Flesch
Messages.Body:
> The "flavor" of the game has already been irrevocably changed by the
> decreed new card text. The people that have been voting for a ban
> do so because the old cards are apparantly unacceptable and the new
> wordings of the cards are worthless.

Setting rhetoric aside...

Why are the new wordings of the cards 'worthless'?

> It is easier to tell a person new to your group, these 5 cards are
> banned than to say read these 2 pages on these 5 cards and then
> read the other 25 pages of errata on this website before you come
> to play.

Straw-man. Nobody is saying that anyone has to do it. It is
easier to play Go-fish than Jyhad. Because it is easier, it
doesn't mean it is better.

Whether or not the text on the proposed cards is changed, there
will still be (and will always be) 25 pages of errata on the
website to read. This is because of the hackneyed manner
in which rulings were decided, made, changed, and amended
over the course of the games' publication.

If it will make it easy to players, type out the new text on
labels, paste them to the cards themselves, and use sleeves.
Yes, they're now marked cards. If playing in a tournament,
then tell the judge first, that this is a newbie and they need
the added help. If you're simply teaching them how to play,
this will be a good way to get them up to speed. (Don't use real
RtI's then; use extra Rats' Warning or Cryptic Missions or
something).

> I would rather see a card officially banned than see that same card
> changed into a new card completely unsupported by card text.

Don't play with the card then. Don't make that decision
for someone else. I hate Direct Interventions. I don't give up
every time someone else uses one.

> But, I agree with you in your belief that they are not broken.

I disagree.

> However, if all players are forced to play with Direct Intervention
> and Sudden Reversal because of the presence of these cards in the
> game, something needs to be done.

Absolutely.

I am firmly a non-banner.

Alan (aj)
